Stop the agent-created skill/shared symlink from dirtying the main checkout and tripping the implement skill dirty-tree gate. The symlink is created by skill bootstrap scripts and is untracked.

## Problem

The 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 is
enforced only by review. Evidence of the gap: WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO decomposed
`database.ts` from 2,584 lines and closed as shipped, yet
`packages/shared/src/database.ts` is now 3,684 lines — the decomposition never
landed on `main` and nothing flagged the regrowth. The same sweep created 12+
sibling god-class items (WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B, WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU,
WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ, ...), each of which can regrow the same way.

## Goal

A cheap, deterministic check (script or test) that fails when a source file
exceeds 1,000 lines, with an explicit, shrinking allow-list for grandfathered
files so the check is green from day one and cannot silently regrow.

## Draft acceptance criteria

1. A check exists (script `scripts/check-file-size.ts` or a vitest unit test)
   that reports every non-test source file > 1,000 lines.
2. Grandfathered files are listed explicitly with their current line count, and
   the check fails if a listed file grows beyond its recorded budget.
3. The check is wired into an existing automated gate (pre-push or CI) without
   adding more than ~2 s to that gate.
4. Retiring an entry is required when an item from the WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7
   sweep completes a decomposition.
5. Documentation updated (`docs/dev/` note) and the existing test suite still
   passes.

data.title: Add a file-size guard so god classes cannot regrow past 1,000 lines

# Worktree Module-Resolution Isolation — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

Two documentation gaps exist: `AGENTS.md` (global and repo copies) contains a
dangling link to `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, and the existing isolation
doc lacks a cross-reference to the node-modules-verification doc. This task
produces the final, authoritative documentation on how worktree module
resolution works and repairs all references.

## Users

- **Agents** running the implement workflow: they need one authoritative doc
  explaining the supported setup and the failure signatures to recognise.
- **Producers** reviewing `in_review` items: they need trust in the gate result
  (green means correct, red names the change).
- **Contributors** debugging stale-`dist` false-reds: they need the failure
  signature and the sanctioned refresh mechanism documented.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New doc created.** `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` documents: (a) the
   module-resolution order in a worktree (node_modules symlink/link farm,
   `@worklog/shared` → main vs worktree `packages/shared`, `main`/`exports` →
   `dist`), (b) the supported way to make `packages/shared` changes visible
   (link farm from SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO), and (c) the stale-dist failure
   signature (e.g. the `spy never called` false red).
2. **AGENTS.md links fixed.** All references to `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
   in `AGENTS.md` and `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` resolve to an existing file (absolute
   path or correct relative path).
3. **Cross-reference added.** `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md`
   links to the new isolation doc.
4. **Constraints stated.** The implement skill's `npm install`-in-worktree ban
   and the no-writes-through-node_modules constraint are stated in the isolation
   doc.
5. **Validation passes.** Markdown link checks and the full project test suite
   pass with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Worktree isolation:** all changes must happen in an `implement.py` worktree.
  Do not edit from the main checkout.
- **No `npm install`** in the worktree (writes through the symlink corrupt the
  main checkout's `node_modules`).
- **Markdown links** must resolve from every document's perspective.

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Link portability:** `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is symlinked to SorraAgents'
  `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`. An absolute path to ContextHub's doc will not be
  portable. **Mitigation:** use an absolute path to the specific user's
  ContextHub checkout (the link is only readable, not served to others).
- **Scope creep:** the doc already exists and is comprehensive; do not rewrite
  it. Only add cross-references and fix links.
- **Stale SorraAgents doc:** SorraAgents has its own shorter version of the doc
  at `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`. The AGENTS.md link currently resolves
  to it. **Decision:** the link should point to ContextHub's more comprehensive
  version; verify the implement skill doesn't also link to the SorraAgents copy.

## Existing State

- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` already exists with substantial content
  (worktrees, sync temp worktrees, guards, filesystem-walk races, main-checkout
  deletions).
- `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md` exists but does not
  cross-reference the isolation doc.
- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` line 40 has `[docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md](docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md)` —
  a relative link that resolves from the repo root but not from the global
  install location.
- `AGENTS.md` in this repo root and `templates/AGENTS.md` do not currently link
  to the isolation doc (the task is about fixing existing dangling links).

## Related Work

- **WL-0MVLK2JNB002E9JQ** — Worktree tests resolve `@worklog/shared` to the main
  checkout's stale dist (the root cause of the problem this docs the fix for).
- **SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO** — SorraAgents item delivering the link-farm mechanism
  (the resolution fix; blocked-by).
- **WL-0MVWK20DK004TQZM** — Recurrence: `packages/shared` wiped from main checkout.
- **WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2** — Worktree node_modules verification (related doc).
- **WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO** — Verify persist write-detection regression tests
  (the `spy never called` false red example).

## Appendix

No clarifying questions — the work item description and related work provide
sufficient detail for implementation.

## Plan review findings (2026-11-02)

Effort/risk pre-check: **Small / Low** (below the planning threshold), so the
plan session reviewed the existing content instead of decomposing it. Review
outcome: **three open questions block completion** — see below. The item is
left at `intake_complete`, awaiting producer answers.

### Corrected existing state (verified during review)

- **`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` does not exist in this repository.** The global agent
  file `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to
  `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`; it is installed by
  **SorraAgents'** `scripts/install_pi.sh` (ContextHub has no such script).
  ContextHub `AGENTS.md` line 3 claims the install comes from "this
  repository's `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`" — inaccurate for ContextHub, and out of
  scope here unless the producer wants it corrected in this item.
- **Nothing to repair in ContextHub `AGENTS.md` / `templates/AGENTS.md`.**
  Neither contains a reference to `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, so the
  "dangling link" exists only in the SorraAgents copy of the global file (its
  relative link is dangling for a reader of `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`, while
  resolving fine inside the SorraAgents checkout).
- **ContextHub `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`** (~230 lines) covers
  implementation worktrees, sync temp worktrees, hook guards, main-checkout
  deletion detection/recovery and repo-wide-walk races, but has **no**
  module-resolution section.
- **`docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md`** has no link
  to the isolation doc (AC3 confirmed outstanding).
- **No markdown link checker exists in ContextHub** — `package.json` has no
  link/lint script and no doc-link test covers `docs/dev/*.md`. AC5's
  "Markdown link checks" therefore needs either one documented manual command
  or a small script/test added by the item.
- **AC4 constraints:** the `npm install`-in-worktree ban is already stated in
  isolation doc §1; the "no writes through `node_modules`" rule is only
  implied ("writes pass through the symlink and corrupt the shared tree"), not
  stated as a constraint.
- **AC1(b) mechanism does not exist yet:** `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` is still
  `open` / `plan_complete`, and `implement.py` today only provides
  `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (plus nested workspace symlinks) — there is no
  link farm. Documentation would describe a workflow that cannot be followed
  yet.

### AC coverage review

| AC | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| AC1(a) resolution order | Ready | Main checkout's `node_modules/@worklog/shared` → `../../packages/shared`; `main`/`exports` → `./dist/*.js` (verified in `packages/shared/package.json`) |
| AC1(b) link-farm setup | **Blocked** | Depends on `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` (Q2) |
| AC1(c) stale-dist signature | Ready | "spy never called" false red — WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO |
| AC2 link repair | **Blocked** | Cross-repo target + authoritative-doc decision (Q1, Q3) |
| AC3 cross-reference | Ready | Small edit |
| AC4 constraints stated | Ready | Small edit |
| AC5 validation | Ready, with gap | No link checker exists; item must add one or document a manual check |

### OPEN QUESTION 1 — scope / repo split (producer, blocking)

AC2 spans two repositories: `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` lives in the SorraAgents
checkout, while this item's constraint requires all changes inside a ContextHub
`implement.py` worktree. Options:

- **A (recommended).** Keep AC2 here in scope but file a separate
  SorraAgents-scoped work item for the `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` edit; a cross-repo
  reference edit cannot ship from a ContextHub worktree.
- **B.** Reword AC2 to ContextHub only (add the isolation-doc link to
  ContextHub `AGENTS.md`) and file the global-link fix against SorraAgents.
- **C.** Explicitly authorise this item to edit both checkouts as a documented
  exception to the worktree constraint.

Why it matters: it determines whether implementation creates one worktree or
two, and whether a SorraAgents item must land first.

### OPEN QUESTION 2 — dependency on an unbuilt mechanism (producer, blocking)

AC1(b) must document the link-farm setup from `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO`, which is
not implemented (`implement.py` still only symlinks `node_modules`). Options:

- **A (recommended).** Mark this item `blocked` on `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` and
  implement once it lands, so the doc describes the mechanism as built and
  testable.
- **B.** Ship AC1(a)/(c), AC3, AC4 now and add AC1(b) as a follow-up child
  after SA lands.
- **C.** Document the intended mechanism now, explicitly labelled "not yet
  implemented".

Why it matters: documenting a non-existent setup would send agents down a path
that silently resolves to the main checkout's stale `dist` — the false-red /
false-green problem this doc is meant to prevent.

### OPEN QUESTION 3 — authoritative doc and link target (producer, blocking)

The intake states the `AGENTS.md` link should point at ContextHub's "more
comprehensive version", but the SorraAgents copy
(`SorraAgents/docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, 416 lines, including the RCA and
test-isolation references) is the longer document and is the one the framework
guidance actually ships with; ContextHub's doc is only longer in
ContextHub-specific guards (main-checkout recovery, walk races). Options:

- **A.** Global link → ContextHub doc by absolute path (as the intake states);
  the SorraAgents doc stays unchanged. Risk: the global agent file then depends
  on one user's checkout layout (the intake already accepts this).
- **B (recommended).** Global link → SorraAgents doc via a repo-portable
  reference (absolute path or a path that stays valid inside that checkout),
  and add the module-resolution section to ContextHub's doc with an explicit
  cross-link between the two.
- **C.** Keep both docs, cross-link them, and state in each which one is
  authoritative for what.

Why it matters: it decides which file AC1's module-resolution section is
authored in, and whether the global link is portable.

### Proposed sequencing (contingent on the answers)

1. Add the missing doc-link check (script or test) proving every `docs/dev/*.md`
   reference resolves — makes AC5 executable rather than manual.
2. Author the AC1 module-resolution section in the doc chosen by Q3.
3. Add the AC3 cross-reference and the AC4 constraint statements.
4. Repair the AC2 references in the repo(s) chosen by Q1, rebasing AC1(b) on
   `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` per Q2.

### Appendix — questions and answers

- Q: "AC2 spans two repositories (SorraAgents `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` vs this
  ContextHub worktree constraint) — which repo(s) should the fix land in?"
  Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer), no evidence yet; options A/B/C
  above.
- Q: "AC1(b) documents the link farm from `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO`, which is not
  implemented — block, split, or document as forward-looking?"
  Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Evidence:
  `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` stage `plan_complete`, `status: open`;
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` has `_ensure_node_modules_symlink`
  only.
- Q: "Which `worktree-isolation.md` is authoritative, and what should the
  global link point at?"
  Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Evidence: ContextHub doc 230
  lines vs SorraAgents doc 416 lines; `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` →
  `SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`.
- Prior answered input reused: intake Appendix states "No clarifying
  questions — the work item description and related work provide sufficient
  detail"; that holds for AC1(a)/(c), AC3, AC4 and does not pre-empt Q1–Q3.

## Plan decisions (2026-11-02) — producer answers and final scope

Producer answered the three open questions raised by the review:

- **Q1 → A.** Keep AC2 in scope here, and file a SorraAgents-scoped work item
  for the `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` edit → **`SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S`** ("Fix dangling
  worktree-isolation.md link in AGENTS_GLOBAL.md (absolute path + ContextHub
  cross-link)"). A global-file change cannot ship from a ContextHub worktree.
- **Q2 → "as you prefer".** Chosen: **B — ship what is ready now, defer the
  link-farm subsection.** Reasoned deviation from the option A I had
  recommended: `wl` reconciles `blocked` → `open` from the dependency-edge
  graph and cross-store edges cannot be recorded yet
  (WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD), so "mark blocked on the SA item" is not a mechanical
  hold here — it would silently look startable. Option B instead delivers
  AC1(a), AC1(c), AC3, AC4 and AC5 now and isolates AC1(b) in a child that
  carries an explicit producer hold.
- **Q3 → B.** The global `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` link targets **SorraAgents'**
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` via an absolute path; **this** repository's
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` carries the module-resolution section and
  cross-links the SorraAgents page (whose own ContextHub cross-link is in
  `SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S`).

### Scope map: acceptance criteria → work item

| AC | Where it is delivered |
|---|---|
| AC1(a) resolution order | `WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU` (module-resolution section) |
| AC1(b) link-farm setup | `WL-0MVZ4IJKL000VFEL` — held pending `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` |
| AC1(c) stale-dist signature | `WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU` |
| AC2 link repair | `SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S` (SorraAgents) — this item tracks it |
| AC3 cross-reference | `WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU` |
| AC4 constraints stated | `WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU` |
| AC5 validation | `WL-0MVZ4I4QR000C1UG` (adds the link check) + changed-scope gate |

### Children (test-first, dependency order)

1. **`WL-0MVZ4I4QR000C1UG`** — *Doc-link resolution check for `docs/dev` and
   `AGENTS.md`* (task; verification first, makes AC5 executable). Startable now.
2. **`WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU`** — *Add module-resolution section to
   `worktree-isolation.md` with AC3 cross-reference and AC4 constraints* (docs;
   depends on 1).
3. **`WL-0MVZ4IJKL000VFEL`** — *Document link-farm setup once
   `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` lands (AC1b)* (docs; depends on 2; held with
   `needsProducerReview=true` until the SA mechanism ships).

### Corrections to this brief's earlier sections

Where the sections above contradict the "Plan review findings" section, the
findings win: there is no `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` in this repository, ContextHub's
`AGENTS.md` / `templates/AGENTS.md` carry no isolation-doc reference to repair,
SorraAgents' copy of the doc is the longer one (not "shorter"), and no Markdown
link checker existed before child 1 created one.

### Sequencing notes for implementation

- Child 1 must land first: it is the verification for every subsequent link
  edit (test-first ordering).
- Child 2 keeps the existing isolation-doc sections untouched (intake risk:
  no rewrite) and adds the `Constraints` block rather than restating §1.
- Child 3 replaces child 2's "current vs pending" note with the shipped
  link-farm description — it must not be started before
  `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` is `in_review`/`completed`.
- `SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S` is independent of children 1–3 and can proceed in
  parallel in the SorraAgents repository.

## Plan changelog (2026-11-05) — re-plan after the link-farm mechanism landed

Effort/risk pre-check: **Small / Low** → below the planning threshold (skip
path). The six review stages ran against the existing content; the 2026-11-02
decomposition is unchanged and reused (no new features invented, no duplicate
children). Only facts were refreshed.

### What changed since 2026-11-02

- **`SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` (SorraAgents, the link-farm mechanism) is now
  `completed` / `in_review`.** `implement.py start` materialises a
  worktree-local link farm (`_materialise_link_farm` /
  `_reconcile_link_farm`), overrides every path-consumed workspace package
  (`@worklog/shared` → the worktree's own `packages/shared`) and reports
  `shared_resolution` / `shared_resolution_ok` in its start JSON. AC1(b) is
  therefore no longer forward-looking: child 3 was re-planned to
  `plan_complete` and is implementable.
- **Child 1** `WL-0MVZ4I4QR000C1UG` (doc-link check) and **child 2**
  `WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU` (module-resolution section + AC3 cross-reference +
  AC4 constraints) are `completed` / `done` (commits `a58a5818`,
  `905b46e1`) → AC1(a), AC1(c), AC3, AC4 and AC5 are delivered.
- **AC2 is delivered cross-repo.** `SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S` (SorraAgents) is
  `completed` / `in_review` (commit `721624cf6`); the installed
  `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` was verified to have zero dangling file links. No
  ContextHub-side work remains for AC2.
- **New fact found in review (folded into child 3, not a new child):**
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` §"Current vs pending: there is no link farm
  yet" and the subtitle/fix 1 of
  `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md` now describe the
  pre-fix world as current. Correcting both is the same edit on the same
  subject as child 3 → child 3's AC1b/AC4/AC5 and Key Files cover it.

### AC coverage review (2026-11-05)

`run_coverage_review` → `recommendation: auto_close`, coverage 20% (1 of 5
parent ACs). Every "gap" maps to an **already-completed** child AC:

| Parent AC | Matched child AC (completed) | Score |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 (new doc) | child 2 — "Resolution order documented (AC1a)" | 0.29 |
| AC2 (AGENTS.md links) | child 1 — "Check exists and runs in the default suite" | 0.23 |
| AC4 (constraints) | child 2 — "Constraints stated (AC4)" | 0.26 |
| AC5 (validation) | child 2 — "Links resolve and the suite is green" | 0.21 |

The scores fall below the 0.4 coverage threshold only because the parent ACs
are long compound sentences; the `resolved_gaps` mapping is semantically
correct. `apply_coverage_review` was therefore **deliberately not applied**: it
would create four `Close coverage gap: …` children that duplicate completed
work, which the plan skill's duplicate-detection rule forbids. The outcome is
recorded here instead — see OPEN QUESTION 4.

### OPEN QUESTION 4 — coverage gate vs duplicate creation (recorded, non-blocking; producer raised no objection)

Option A (taken) stands. Assumption recorded rather than invented: the producer
answered the hold-release question with **A** on 2026-11-05 and gave no
instruction on this question, so it is left as a documented deviation to be
revisited if the producer prefers B or C.

The helper reaches `auto_close` on this parent and would create four duplicate
children even though the semantic coverage is complete.

- **A (taken).** Advance to `plan_complete`, record the mapping above, create
  nothing. Risk: the gate's own record shows 20% coverage for a covered plan.
- **B.** Rewrite the parent `## Acceptance Criteria` as the seven-item
  decomposition the scope map below already defines. Risk: it inverts the gate
  (parent ACs copied from children) and drops the met-outside-the-tree AC2
  record.
- **C.** Accept the four auto-created children and close them as duplicates of
  the completed ones. Risk: four permanently closed duplicate items as noise.

### Appendix — questions and answers (2026-11-05)

- Q: "The link-farm mechanism (`SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO`) is now
  `completed`/`in_review`, which is exactly what child `WL-0MVZ4IJKL000VFEL`
  was held for. Should its producer hold (`needsProducerReview`) be cleared so
  it can be dispatched?"
  Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): **A — clear the hold now.** Final: A.
  Evidence: `wl show SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` → `completed` / `in_review`;
  `implement.py` ships `_materialise_link_farm` / `_shared_resolution_check`.
  Applied: `WL-0MVZ4IJKL000VFEL` has `needsProducerReview=false`, no assignee,
  `open` / `plan_complete` → dispatchable. Option B (wait for a manual probe)
  was declined; the probe survives as that child's AC3, so the evidence is
  produced by the work itself.
- Prior answers reused, not re-asked: Q1 → A, Q2 → "as you prefer" → B,
  Q3 → B (all 2026-11-02, see "Plan decisions" above).

### Sequencing notes (unchanged)

- Children 1 and 2 already landed; child 3 is the only open child and must not
  be started before its producer hold is cleared (its own AC1b is what proves
  the farm works, so it is self-verifying once started).
- `SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S` (AC2) is complete; nothing awaits it.
- The parent stays `open` / `plan_complete` with its `Map` producer hold: a
  child is non-terminal, so the parent is not advanced to `in_review`.

# Refactor guard: worklist split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B — decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `worklist.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely without touching any existing test file and
without a reviewer having to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 require: every production module ≤1,000 lines, an
unchanged public surface at `./worklist.js`, unmodified test files, no new
circular imports, and a single `WorkItemListState` declaration. Nothing in the
repo enforces these for `worklist.ts` today. The `downtime-worker` series
already built exactly this machinery for its own split
(`packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` + `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`);
this child reuses it rather than duplicating it.

Facts captured at plan time (2026-10-30, `dev`, `worklist.ts` = 7,899 lines):

- **36 consumer files** import from `./worklist.js`/`./worklist`: 2 production
  (`index.ts` → `getTermSize`, `runWorklistTui`; `fetcher.ts` → `STAGES`,
  `Stage`) and 34 test files, of which **24** are `worklist*.test.ts` suites.
- **66 distinct symbols** are imported across those consumers; the other 23 of
  the 89 current exports are unused outside the module and become internal
  (parent AC2).
- `WorkItemListState` is declared **once** (`worklist.ts:490`) — the single
  owner AC5 protects.
- `runWorklistTui` is declared once (`worklist.ts:5581`, `export async function`)
  and must stay at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical signature
  (child WL-0MVND6MQS000L01W).
- The live static import graph already contains one large component that
  includes `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
  (`CYCLE_BASELINE` in `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`). It is
  pre-existing and out of scope; what the gate forbids is a **new** cycle member
  or a new **runtime** cycle (parent AC4).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts`
   (vitest) exists and passes on the current tree **before any production code
   moves**; no existing test file is modified (parent AC3).
2. Committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` records
   the 66 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation command,
   source commit, timestamp, scanned globs).
3. **Public-surface gate:** every baseline symbol is still exported by
   `./worklist.js` (value or type), and every symbol the live consumers import
   from the barrel is exported by it — so a lost or trimmed re-export fails the
   suite (parent AC2).
4. **Single state-owner gate:** exactly one production
   `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module declares `WorkItemListState`
   (parent AC5), mirroring the `dispatchInFlightCount` gate.
5. **Barrel/cycle gate:** no production `worklist.*.ts` module contains a
   runtime (value) import of `./worklist.js` (nor of `./index.js`); the static
   import graph of `worklist*.ts` modules contains no cycle outside the recorded
   baseline allowlist (parent AC4).
6. **Size gate:** every production `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module is
   ≤1,000 lines, excluding an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains
   only `'worklist.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever
   shrinks (it must remain a subset of the plan-time list). The final barrel
   child empties it (parent AC1).
7. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a duplicated
   `WorkItemListState`, a new cycle) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not
   assumed.
8. **Reuse, do not fork, the scanner:** extend
   `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` minimally so the barrel path, the
   module-family matcher and the single-owner declaration name are injectable
   (each defaulting to today's `downtime-worker` behaviour). The existing
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` and
   `downtime-worker.split-baseline.json` must stay **byte-identical and green** —
   duplicating the 28k-line scanner is not acceptable.
9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite and the
   untouched `downtime-worker` guard.
10. A comment on this item records the baseline generation command and the
    gate-to-parent-AC mapping.

## Minimal implementation

1. Parametrise `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`: accept a
   `barrel`/`family`/`declarationName` target (defaults unchanged) in
   `isSplitFamilyFile`, `splitFamilyModules`, `findBarrelValueImports`,
   `findSplitFamilyCycles` and `findDispatchInFlightDeclarations`; add a
   `--target worklist` branch to the `--write-baseline` CLI.
2. Generate the baseline: scan `src/**/*.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/*.ts` for
   `import … from './worklist.js'`, normalise `type ` prefixes, dedupe, sort →
   `worklist.split-baseline.json` with provenance fields (expect 66 symbols).
3. Write `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` with the five gates (exports,
   single-owner, cycle/barrel, size+allowlist, baseline provenance), each as a
   separately named `it()` so failures are legible.
4. Add the negative-case fixtures (temp files under `os.tmpdir()` or inline
   sources parsed by the same helpers) and assert each gate reports a failure.
5. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` from the guard's helper section so the final child
   (`WL-0MVND6OOL004SK9N`) can empty it in one line.
6. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope); record the guard output in a comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` — new
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` — minimal parametrisation (defaults preserved)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — read-only (no edits in this child)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` — must stay unchanged and green

## Constraints

- Additive only: adding a test file and a parametrisation hook does not violate
  parent AC3 ("no test file is modified").
- No production `worklist*.ts` edits in this child — it lands first, alone.
- No new runtime dependencies (`typescript` is already used by `scan.ts`).

## Dependencies

None — first child; every extraction child is blocked by this one.

## Notes

- Test-writing guidance: `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
- Precedent: `WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E` (downtime-worker split guard) — same shape,
  same AC numbering, already green on `dev`.

data.description:
# Make groupings stable

## Problem statement

When the herdr selection list re-sorts on refresh, items sometimes move from
one group to another even though nothing about them changed materially. This
causes disconcerting movement in the list. The list should only change when
the underlying items change in a material way (e.g. a new key file is added,
or the priority changes). Additionally, items should sort in priority order —
all high items ahead of medium, all medium ahead of low.

## Users

- **Herdr users / producers** who watch the worklist to decide what to work
  on next. A stable list lets them track where work sits; gratuitous movement
  breaks their mental model of the queue.
- **Producers reviewing the in-review queue** who rely on a predictable
  within-group order to find the most important work first.

User story: *As a Herdr user, I want the worklist grouping and ordering to be
a stable function of the items themselves, so that an item only changes
group when its content (key files, priority, stage/status) or the item set
changes — and within each group, high-priority items always rank above
medium, which rank above low.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Group assignment is **content-deterministic**: for a fixed set of items
      with fixed key files / priority / stage / status, the group each item
      lands in is identical regardless of the order in which the items are
      presented to the grouping algorithm (canonical ordering applied before
      the greedy first-fit packing). A transient change such as an
      `updatedAt` timestamp (comment added, audit run) must never change an
      item's group.
- [ ] An item's group membership changes **only** when a material input
      changes: its key files section, its priority, its stage/status, or the
      item set itself (item added/removed). Verified by a stability test
      that perturbs non-material inputs (`updatedAt`, input order) and
      asserts group labels/numbers are unchanged.
- [ ] Within each group (Critical Group N and Group N), items sort by
      **priority first (high → medium → low)**, then by the existing stage
      sub-order (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining), then by
      id — so all high items appear ahead of all medium items, which appear
      ahead of all low items. The `in_review` 6-bucket comparator already
      sorts priority-first and keeps that behaviour.
- [ ] The change is applied **and kept in sync** in both mirrors: core
      `wl next` / `wl worklist` grouping (`src/commands/grouping.ts`,
      `src/worklist-selection.ts`) and the herdr plugin copy
      (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`); shared grouping tests cover both
      copies.
- [ ] `wl next -n N` and the herdr worklist still emit the canonical section
      order (Critical Group N → Group N → Idea → Other → In Review) with no
      regression in existing grouping/smart-selection behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
      comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Greedy first-fit file-path conflict detection is retained — the change
  makes it order-independent, it does not replace the packing strategy.
- Herdr plugin has zero npm dependencies and cannot import from
  `src/commands/`; the mirror must stay a self-contained pure duplication
  (per WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B decision Q2c).
- The always-show-mandatory guarantee of `selectWorkItems`
  (`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`) is preserved — grouping only
  reorders and stamps, never filters or drops items.
- Default `maxGroups` of 3 for file-path-based groups is unchanged.

## Existing state

- `regroupWorkItems` (herdr) / `selectBrowseFeed` (core) recompute group
  assignments on every refresh from the merged selection.
- `groupItemsByFilePaths` is a greedy first-fit over items **in input
  order**; the input order fluctuates with `updatedAt` (comment/audit
  churn), so the same item set can pack into different groups across
  refreshes. That is the root cause of the observed group hopping.
- Within-group ordering (`compareGroupableItems`) currently sorts by stage
  sub-order first (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining), then
  priority; `in_review` items already sort priority-first.

## Desired change

1. Make `groupItemsByFilePaths` (and hence `assignItemGroups`) a pure
   function of the item content: sort/canonicalise the input items by a
   stable content-derived key before greedy packing, so group membership
   depends only on ids, key files, priority and stage/status — not on
   transient ordering.
2. Make priority the **primary** within-group sort key in
   `compareGroupableItems` (both mirrors), keeping the stage sub-order as
   the secondary key.
3. Keep the two mirrors in sync and extend the grouping tests in both
   locations with stability assertions (order perturbation + non-material
   input perturbation must not change group membership or ordering).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — core `groupItemsByFilePaths` / `assignItemGroups` / `compareGroupableItems`; canonicalise input order; priority-first within-group sort.
- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — core `selectBrowseFeed` grouping pipeline consuming `assignItemGroups`.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — mirrored plugin copy of the same algorithm; must stay in sync.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems`; input order source feeding `regroupWorkItems` (contract only — no functional change expected unless needed for canonicalisation).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts` — callers of `regroupWorkItems`.
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — core grouping tests; add stability assertions.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — plugin grouping tests; mirror stability assertions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Within-group order change is intentional but observable:** making priority
  the primary within-group sort key changes which item of a group renders
  first (stage sub-order becomes secondary). Existing tests in
  `grouping.test.ts` / `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` that assert the old
  stage-first order must be updated deliberately, not incidentally.
- **Canonicalisation key must be content-derived:** the pre-pack sort key
  (e.g. priority + stage + id) must never include timestamps or insertion
  order, or the instability simply moves to the new key.
- **Assumption — "material change" definition:** key files (the `**Key Files:**`
  section), priority, stage/status, or item-set membership. Description prose
  outside the Key Files section already cannot affect grouping
  (`extractFilePaths` reads only that section) and stays non-material.
- **Scope-creep guard:** out-of-scope opportunities (stable group *labels*
  across renumbering, configurable `maxGroups`) are recorded as related/future
  work, not implemented here.

## Related work

- WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ — Rewrite `assignItemGroups` + `next.ts` ordering (completed; produced the current grouping spec this item stabilises).
- WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW — Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order) (completed; established section order + `regroupWorkItems`).
- WL-0MUY1CSQG007TCYX — actively-worked items derived from `status === 'in-progress'` (affects group membership inputs).
- WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G — in_review priority-first ordering (precedent for priority-first within-group sort).

### Related work (automated report)

Low-relevance automatic matches (find-related): WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C (Bubble
up critical items), WL-0MRSGMTYY0062WFJ (audit-set fail hard), WL-0MLGTWT4S1X4HDD9
(needs-producer-review filter) — adjacent selection-list behaviour, no AC
overlap with this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should priority ordering apply? (A) within each group only, (B) globally across the whole list, (C) both" — Answer (producer): **A — within each group only**. Source: interactive reply (intake round, recommended option accepted).
- Q2: "Stability definition — (A) content-deterministic grouping via canonical sort before fit, (B) keep packing, only stabilise within-group ordering" — Answer (producer): **A — content-deterministic grouping**. Source: interactive reply (recommended option accepted).
- Q3: "Scope of the change — (A) both mirrors kept in sync, (B) herdr only, (C) core only" — Answer (producer): **A — both, kept in sync**. Source: interactive reply (recommended option accepted). Research: confirmed the duplicate lives at `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` per WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B Q2c.
data.title: Make groupings stable
